regulation: Multiple: PDMA, Sunshine Act, HIPAA, FDA 21 CFR Part 11

rules.rule: PDMA (Prescription Drug Marketing Act) — Sample Distribution
rules.description: Pharmaceutical samples must be tracked from manufacturer to HCP with full chain of custody. Requires written request from licensed practitioner.
rules.implementation: Sample Management must capture: (1) Written request (signature), (2) Lot tracking from distribution to delivery, (3) Reconciliation of physical inventory, (4) Loss/theft reporting.

rules.rule: Sunshine Act (Open Payments) — HCP Payment Tracking
rules.description: Manufacturers must report payments and transfers of value to physicians/teaching hospitals to CMS annually. Covers meals, travel, consulting fees, speaker programs, research grants.
rules.implementation: Events Management must track: (1) Each transfer of value by type, (2) HCP NPI number linkage, (3) Aggregate spend per HCP per year, (4) CMS-format export. This is the largest gap for most migrations — source platforms often have native Sunshine Act reporting; target may require custom build or integration.
rules.penalty: $10,000-$100,000 per failure to report, up to $1M for knowing failures

rules.description: If CRM stores any PHI (patient data, prescription data, health information), HIPAA Security Rule applies.
rules.implementation: For most life sciences CRM implementations, HIPAA is limited scope — CRM typically stores HCP data (not patient data). However: (1) Any patient support programs that store patient identifiers trigger HIPAA, (2) Analytics features pulling prescription data must be HIPAA-compliant, (3) BAA (Business Associate Agreement) required with platform provider.
affected_modules: All modules if patient data present
rules.penalty: $100-$50,000 per violation, up to $1.5M per year per violation category

rules.description: Electronic records and signatures used in place of paper records must meet specific requirements: audit trails, access controls, electronic signature validation.
rules.implementation: Affects sample management signature capture: (1) Electronic signature must be linked to unique individual, (2) Signature records must be tamper-evident, (3) Audit trail must capture creation, modification, deletion of regulated records. Target platform's Field Audit Trail + Shield Encryption can meet Part 11 requirements.
rules.penalty: Warning letter, consent decree, criminal prosecution

rules: CCPA/CPRA adds data privacy rights similar to GDPR for California residents
Prescriber Confidentiality Law restricts use of prescriber-identified data for marketing
Gift ban: no meals, gifts, or entertainment to HCPs
Affects visit and event tracking requirements

migration_notes: US migrations from source platforms typically have good Sunshine Act / PDMA coverage. Key risks during migration: (1) Sample audit trail continuity — ensure no gaps in chain of custody records, (2) Sunshine Act reporting history — transfer or maintain access to historical spend data for CMS lookback periods, (3) Electronic signature records must be preserved in a way that meets Part 11 — don't just migrate the flag, migrate the signature image/certificate.
